blueprint_concepts: Tangent and normal to a circle
Length of tangent and power of a point wrt a circle

concept_use.Tangent and normal to a circle: The tangent L at T is 3x + 4y = 25, and P on it gives PT as a tangent segment of C1.
concept_use.Length of tangent and power of a point w: PT^2 = S1(P) is the power of P (length of tangent) with respect to C1; the tangent length to C2 is sqrt(S2(P)); equality puts P on the radical axis.

english: Let $T=(3,4)$ and let $L$ be the tangent to the circle $C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ at $T$. Let $P$ be the point on $L$ such that the length of the tangent drawn from $P$ to the circle $C_{2}:x^{2}+y^{2}-4x+2y+1=0$ is equal to $PT$. Then $PT$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $T=(3,4)$ है तथा $L$ वृत्त $C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ के बिन्दु $T$ पर स्पर्श रेखा है। माना $P$ रेखा $L$ पर वह बिन्दु है जिससे वृत्त $C_{2}:x^{2}+y^{2}-4x+2y+1=0$ पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखा की लम्बाई $PT$ के बराबर है। तब $PT$ बराबर है
solution: $L$: $3x+4y=25$. Since $P$ is on the tangent at $T$, $PT$ is the tangent length from $P$ to $C_{1}$, so $PT^{2}=S_{1}(P)$
Condition: $S_{1}(P)=S_{2}(P)$, so $P$ lies on the radical axis $S_{1}-S_{2}=0$: $4x-2y-26=0$, i.e. $2x-y=13$
solution_full: Any point $P$ on this tangent sees $C_{1}$ along the tangent $PT$, so the length of the tangent from $P$ to $C_{1}$ is $PT$, and $PT^{2}=S_{1}(P)=x^{2}+y^{2}-25$.
The length of the tangent from $P$ to $C_{2}$ is $\sqrt{S_{2}(P)}$. The condition is $S_{1}(P)=S_{2}(P)$.
$P$ is outside $C_{2}$: $S_{2}(7,1)=49+1-28+2+1=25>0$, so the tangent exists and has length $5$.
originality_note: New: the tangent length to the first circle is hidden as the distance PT along its own tangent line, so the equal-tangent condition becomes an intersection of that tangent with the radical axis (way 5). Closest known: point from which tangents to two circles are equal (radical axis). Different because: one tangent length is not given as a tangent length but as a distance along a tangent line, and the student must recognise it.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, curve and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, the options have one form and the Hindi mirrors the English. Checked that P is unique (two non-parallel lines) and outside C2. Answer 5 at (D) as planned. No change.
key_step: Recognise PT as the tangent length from P to C1, so P is on the radical axis S1 - S2 = 0.
justification: A short chain of standard results (tangent at a point, tangent length as power, radical axis) with one recognition step; comparable to the routine L2 circle anchors such as 2026-P1-Q2 (L2).
